title: WhatsApp direct through Meta's Cloud API behind the existing messaging interface
goal: Send and receive WhatsApp messages through Meta directly instead of paying a reseller fee on every message.
why: COST-MODEL item 2: Twilio adds $0.005 to every WhatsApp message in and out (about ₹0.48), on top of Meta's fee; no Meta Cloud API code exists; services/voip-provider.ts defines MessagingProvider with Twilio and Plivo implementations only.
steps: meta-whatsapp.ts implements MessagingProvider for WhatsApp: send text inside the 24 h window, send template (name, language, components) with category for metering, media by URL; Graph API base https://graph.facebook.com/v<version>/<phone_number_id>/messages via fetch; access token per platform (WHATSAPP_META_TOKEN) or per agency (encrypted, R108) when the agency brings its own WABA.

Inbound webhook /api/v1/webhooks/inbound/meta/whatsapp: GET verification (hub.mode, hub.verify_token, hub.challenge), POST with X-Hub-Signature-256 (HMAC-SHA256 of raw body with the app secret) verified; tenant resolved from the receiving phone_number_id through tenant_channel_addresses; messages go through the existing inbound ingest (services/inbound/ingest.ts) and statuses through the delivery tracking path, deduped on Meta message id.
Provider selection per agency in integrations settings (twilio | meta) with Meta as the default for new agencies when the platform token is configured; Twilio stays available.
tests: backend/test/meta-whatsapp.test.ts: verification challenge; signed inbound text creates an inbound message and lead flow as the Twilio path does; bad signature -> 401; status delivered updates the message; template send body shape (mocked fetch) includes category; metering called with whatsapp_utility vs whatsapp_marketing correctly.
acceptance: Inbound and outbound WhatsApp work through Meta in tests with the same downstream behaviour as Twilio.
gate: cd backend && npx vitest run   # pass: 0 failed files and passed >= the last merged count (1296 on 2026-10-14)
cd desktop && npx tsc --noEmit && npx tsc -p electron/tsconfig.json --noEmit
cd desktop && npx vitest run   # pass: 0 failing files, passed >= last merged count (1294 on 2026-10-14)

cd desktop && E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3110 E2E_API_URL=http://localhost:8797/api/v1 npx playwright test e2e/communication-inbox.spec.ts e2e/whatsapp-campaigns.spec.ts e2e/webhooks-integrations.spec.ts
goLiveVerify: Meta Business verification, WABA, phone number registration, template approvals, app secret and verify token; real message round trip.
notes: Before editing read: this batch file, docs/readiness/READINESS-PLAN.md sections 0 and the design note for this area, desktop/audit/fix/FIX-PLAN.md sections 3-4 (executor rules, worktree bootstrap with node_modules junctions; never npm install inside a worktree unless the batch adds a dependency, and then only in the main checkout by the orchestrator).

Backend tests follow the existing pattern (see backend/test/voip-callbacks.test.ts): import env, createExecutionContext, waitOnExecutionContext, applyD1Migrations from cloudflare:test; applyD1Migrations(env.MASTER_DB, env.TEST_MIGRATIONS) in beforeAll; POST /api/v1/test/reset; call worker.fetch(request, env, ctx). isolatedStorage is false and singleWorker true, so use unique ids/emails per test file.

Bulk seeding in tests or e2e (many leads, messages or payments) triggers automation recipes; set settings.automations_paused = true for that tenant first (PUT /api/v1/automations/pause or the setting row), then restore it.
